chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Al-Wassha', from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I saw him fasting on Friday, so I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, the people claim that it is a day of Eid (festival). He said, 'No, indeed it is a day of modesty and calm.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is the one upon which action is taken, and the first one (the earlier narration), its chain consists of the men of the Sunnis (general people), and it is not acted upon.

key_terms.الْمَعْمُولُ عَلَيْهِ: Upon which action is taken (preferred ruling)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on fasting on Friday and how is it described in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the jurisprudential preference for fasting on Friday as a day of humility (khafḍ) and composure (da'ah), countering the popular notion of it being a festive Eid. Shaykh al-Tusi highlights that this specific chain is the operative ruling (al-ma'mul bihi), distinguishing it from earlier reports with weaker, non-Shia (al-'ammah) narrators. This distinction underscores the Shia methodology of prioritizing reliable chains over general consensus when determining legal practice.
